Automatic: the built-in Turnip on an Adreno 8xx or 7xx, the system driver on any other GPU. Built-in Turnip: always (for an Adreno 8xx or 7xx). System driver: the phone\'s own. Custom driver: a driver file you choose.
Full info shows a bar at the top: GPU and CPU load, memory, power draw, temperature and an FPS graph. Handy to see what slows the game down.

Xenia emulates the Xbox 360\'s graphics chip: the most tested way. Native draws the game\'s scenes with Vulkan directly, without that emulation; it is new, so if something looks wrong, switch back to Xenia and send a bug report. Takes effect the next time the game starts.
Writes the GPU\'s measurements into the game\'s log (a little slower). Turn it on, play the part that misbehaves, then Report a bug.

Touch: press and drag anywhere free on the left half to move; swipe the right half to look. The camera stops as soon as your finger stops moving. On-screen buttons and the D-pad remain available. Adjust camera sensitivity in the game settings, when supported.

XDroid360 is MIT-licensed, except its native renderer, which is GPL-3.0. Dragon Age: Origins' game library links it, so that library and this app are GPL-3.0 as a whole (source: github.com/udarmolota/XDroid360 at the release's tag). It carries:

• The native renderer: nfsmw-android by codepdbh, after nfsmw-nx (StevensND), NFSMW-Recompiled (madelrandel-blip) and NFSMW-Recompiled-Mobile (victorgbd) (GPL-3.0); ReXGlue SDK (BSD 3-Clause)
• SDL 3 (zlib)
• Mesa Turnip, StevenMXZ's Gen8 build (MIT)
• liblinkernsbypass (BSD 2-Clause)
• AndroidX, Material Components, Material icons (Apache-2.0)
• LLVM clang, lld, libc++, libunwind, compiler-rt (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exception)
• Android NDK sysroot (Apache-2.0, BSD; Android SDK License Agreement)
• XenonRecomp, the recompiler the launcher runs (GPL-2.0+ as a whole, for its binutils disassembler; source: github.com/hedge-dev/XenonRecomp at ddd128bc plus scripts/patch_recompiler.py at b7bd9be of github.com/udarmolota/Dragon-Age-Origins-Recomp-Android)
• shaderlib, the shader translator the launcher runs (GPL-3.0 as a whole), with XenosRecomp, fmt, xxHash (MIT, BSD)
• DirectXShaderCompiler (University of Illinois/NCSA), with SPIRV-Tools, SPIRV-Headers, DirectX-Headers (Apache-2.0, MIT)
• XenonUtils (MIT)
• DAORecomp by 96dot, SoDRecomp (MIT)
• Xenia (BSD 3-Clause)
• Vulkan-Headers, VulkanMemoryAllocator, glslang, fmt, xxHash, Snappy, Dear ImGui, toml++, SIMDe, FidelityFX (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD)
• FFmpeg 8.0, has207/FFmpeg (LGPL 2.1+; source: github.com/has207/FFmpeg)
• libmspack (LGPL 2.1), tiny-AES-c (Unlicense), TinySHA1

The full texts are in the licenses/ folders of the kit and the game profiles inside the APK, and in NOTICE.md at github.com/udarmolota/XDroid360.

XDroid360: Xbox 360 games on Android, built on DAORecomp by 96dot, Xenia's Vulkan backend and Mesa's Turnip. Made with the help of AI.

Installing a game

XDroid360 has no games in it: you add your own copy, and the phone builds it.

1. Copy the game to the phone: the disc image (.iso, or a .zip with it) for Dragon Age: Origins and Mass Effect; for State of Decay, a .zip of its folder from your console\'s storage.
2. Tap + and pick the file. The card shows which game it is and the space it needs.
3. Tap Build. Dragon Age and State of Decay take 5–20 minutes, Mass Effect 30–60. You can lock the phone meanwhile; don\'t swipe the app away.
4. Tap Play.

Games and editions

Dragon Age: Origins: the English/Italian/Spanish disc, disc 1 of the Ultimate Edition, the Russian or the German edition. Mass Effect: its disc image. State of Decay: its folder with the DLC and Title Update 6. The launcher tells you if your edition isn\'t supported yet.

DLC and title updates (Dragon Age)

Open the Import tab, pick Dragon Age, and add your DLC packages (files from a console, a .zip of them, or the Ultimate Edition\'s second disc). Warden\'s Keep, The Stone Prisoner, Return to Ostagar and the armour packs work right away. Awakening and the later campaigns also need Title Update 7 for your edition: import it the same way, then run Update game.

After a launcher update

When the launcher brings a newer version of a game, Play asks to update it (a red note shows on its card too). Updating keeps your files, saves and settings. You can also run it from ⋮ → Update game.

Game settings (⚙ on the card)

Renderer: Native draws the game directly with Vulkan and is much faster; Xenia (emulated) is the fallback if Native shows something wrong.
Driver: Automatic uses the built-in Turnip on Adreno 7xx/8xx and the phone\'s own driver elsewhere. You can install another one from the menu.
Frame rate: 30 is cooler and kinder to the battery; 60 is smoother.
Widescreen (Dragon Age only): fills the screen\'s width instead of black bars; turn it off if the picture looks wrong.
Texture detail: lower it if the game runs out of memory.

Controls and saves

A Bluetooth or USB gamepad works as is; the on-screen controls hide while one is used. Controls edits the on-screen layout for each game. Export and Import back up and move saves and layouts.

If something goes wrong

• White or black screen: try the other driver (Automatic, Built-in Turnip, System) or the other renderer.
• Building fails: check the free space the card asked for, then tap Retry; a failed step often passes the second time.
• Crashes or glitches: send Report a bug from the menu; the logs are attached.

Antivirus warnings

Some scanners (and Chrome\'s download check) flag XDroid360: it carries a compiler that builds the game on your phone. That is a false positive. Download it only from GitHub, and check its certificate fingerprint there.
